# dtfttp

> Copies a triangular matrix from Rectangular Full Packed (RFP) format to standard packed format (TP).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dtfttp from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dtfttp';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dtfttp( transr, uplo, N, ARF, strideARF, AP, strideAP ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `transr` | `"no-transpose" \| "transpose"` | Specifies whether `ARF` is in normal or transposed format (`'no-transpose'` or `'transpose'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the matrix is upper or lower triangular (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ARF` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | Input array in RFP format |
| ↳ `strideARF` | `integer` | Stride length for `ARF` |
| `AP` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | **out** · Output array in standard packed format |
| ↳ `strideAP` | `integer` | Stride length for `AP` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `transr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: `ARF` is in Normal format;
  -   `= 'T'`: `ARF` is in Transpose format;
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `ARF`: On entry, the upper or lower triangular matrix A stored in RFP format. For a further discussion see Notes below.
- `AP`: On exit, the upper or lower triangular matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-transpose", "transpose"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dtfttp.ndarray(
    transr, uplo,
    N,
    ARF, strideARF, offsetARF,
    AP, strideAP, offsetAP
) → integer
```

Copy a triangular matrix from Rectangular Full Packed (RFP) format to standard packed format (TP).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `transr` | `"no-transpose" \| "transpose"` | Specifies whether `ARF` is in normal or transposed format (`'no-transpose'` or `'transpose'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the matrix is upper or lower triangular (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ARF` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | Input array in RFP format |
| ↳ `strideARF` | `integer` | Stride length for `ARF` |
| ↳ `offsetARF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `ARF` |
| `AP` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | **out** · Output array in standard packed format |
| ↳ `strideAP` | `integer` | Stride length for `AP` |
| ↳ `offsetAP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AP` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `transr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: `ARF` is in Normal format;
  -   `= 'T'`: `ARF` is in Transpose format;
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `ARF`: On entry, the upper or lower triangular matrix A stored in RFP format. For a further discussion see Notes below.
- `AP`: On exit, the upper or lower triangular matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-transpose", "transpose"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dtfttp from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dtfttp';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const ARF = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const AP = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dtfttp( 'no-transpose', 'upper', N, ARF, 1, AP, 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dtfttp.ndarray( 'no-transpose', 'upper', N, ARF, 1, 0, AP, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DTFTTP`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DTFTTP copies a triangular matrix A from rectangular full packed format (TF) to standard packed format (TP).

### Further Details

We first consider Rectangular Full Packed (RFP) Format when N is even. We give an example where $N = 6$.

```text
AP is Upper             AP is Lower
```

```text
00 01 02 03 04 05       00
   11 12 13 14 15       10 11
      22 23 24 25       20 21 22
         33 34 35       30 31 32 33
            44 45       40 41 42 43 44
               55       50 51 52 53 54 55
```

Let `TRANSR = 'N'`. RFP holds `AP` as follows: For `UPLO = 'U'` the upper trapezoid A(0:5,0:2) consists of the last three columns of `AP` upper. The lower triangle A(4:6,0:2) consists of the transpose of the first three columns of `AP` upper. For `UPLO = 'L'` the lower trapezoid A(1:6,0:2) consists of the first three columns of `AP` lower. The upper triangle A(0:2,0:2) consists of the transpose of the last three columns of `AP` lower. This covers the case N even and `TRANSR = 'N'`.

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
03 04 05                33 43 53
13 14 15                00 44 54
23 24 25                10 11 55
33 34 35                20 21 22
00 44 45                30 31 32
01 11 55                40 41 42
02 12 22                50 51 52
```

Now let `TRANSR = 'T'`. RFP A in both `UPLO` cases is just the transpose of RFP A above. One therefore gets:

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
03 13 23 33 00 01 02    33 00 10 20 30 40 50
04 14 24 34 44 11 12    43 44 11 21 31 41 51
05 15 25 35 45 55 22    53 54 55 22 32 42 52
```

We then consider Rectangular Full Packed (RFP) Format when N is odd. We give an example where $N = 5$.

```text
AP is Upper                 AP is Lower
```

```text
00 01 02 03 04              00
   11 12 13 14              10 11
      22 23 24              20 21 22
         33 34              30 31 32 33
            44              40 41 42 43 44
```

Let `TRANSR = 'N'`. RFP holds `AP` as follows: For `UPLO = 'U'` the upper trapezoid A(0:4,0:2) consists of the last three columns of `AP` upper. The lower triangle A(3:4,0:1) consists of the transpose of the first two columns of `AP` upper. For `UPLO = 'L'` the lower trapezoid A(0:4,0:2) consists of the first three columns of `AP` lower. The upper triangle A(0:1,1:2) consists of the transpose of the last two columns of `AP` lower. This covers the case N odd and `TRANSR = 'N'`.

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
02 03 04                00 33 43
12 13 14                10 11 44
22 23 24                20 21 22
00 33 34                30 31 32
01 11 44                40 41 42
```

Now let `TRANSR = 'T'`. RFP A in both `UPLO` cases is just the transpose of RFP A above. One therefore gets:

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
02 12 22 00 01             00 10 20 30 40 50
03 13 23 33 11             33 11 21 31 41 51
04 14 24 34 44             43 44 22 32 42 52
```

</section>
